blueprint_refs: CALIBRATION IS SBI (NPE) AND MUST MATCH THE CURRENT HOSP PIPELINE
Train NPE posterior p(θ|x) on the simulated pairs; then condition on x_o, sample posterior, and take posterior mean as optimized_parameters.

evidence.metrics: Calibration loss decreases strongly (~298 -> ~23), but train/val/test losses remain extremely high and unchanged (train_loss=858.48, val_loss=862.25, test_loss=843.16).

reflection.error_identification: Despite successful minimization of the calibrator's internal training objective, end-to-end evaluation losses do not improve at all, indicating the calibration objective is not aligned with the simulator-to-metrics pipeline.
reflection.root_cause_analysis: The calibrator models q(theta|x) as a diagonal Gaussian with a single-pass conditioning and uses its mean as optimized_theta. This is not equivalent to the intended SBI NPE workflow in the blueprint, and it can learn a miscalibrated mapping that reduces NLL on simulated pairs without producing a theta that minimizes downstream trajectory MSE. Additionally, the network is trained to regress the entire posterior from standardized x without explicit amortized posterior sampling/checks, making it prone to 'good NLL / bad downstream' behavior.
reflection.correct_approach: In NPEGaussianCalibrator.fit: (1) replace the diagonal-Gaussian posterior surrogate with a loss/objective directly aligned to the evaluation metric, or (2) implement a closer SBI-like NPE flow using a conditional density estimator that supports sampling and then compute posterior mean from samples at x_o. If SBI libraries are not allowed, approximate NPE more faithfully by: training a conditional normalizing flow or mixture density network (not single Gaussian), and validating by sampling multiple theta from q(theta|x_o), rolling out multiple trajectories, and selecting theta that minimizes validation-style MSE on the observation trajectory summary (train_states[0]). Keep the final selection deterministic and based on the same 7-D flattened x used by evaluation.
reflection.key_insight: If the calibrator’s training loss improves but evaluation loss is flat, the inference objective is misaligned; add posterior sampling + simulator-in-the-loop selection or use a richer conditional density model so optimized parameters actually minimize the downstream metric.

blueprint_refs: day_index ... allows non-stationary arrival processes by day/time_step if supported by data
Fit mean admissions per day per disease; optionally bucket day/time_step to capture non-stationarity.

evidence.metrics: Very large occupancy/alive-count errors dominate val_loss (val_loss_per_dim: icu_occupancy=1262.57, total_alive=3106.22). A stationary Poisson + stationary LOS often cannot match time-varying census patterns.

reflection.error_identification: The simulator likely cannot reproduce changing occupancy/alive dynamics over time, leading to large per-dimension MSE, especially for total_alive and ICU occupancy.
reflection.root_cause_analysis: HospitalFlowModel.rollout uses constant per-disease Poisson arrival rates (parameters.arrival_lambda[disease_id]) independent of day/time_step. The blueprint explicitly allows day/time_step as a covariate (e.g., day buckets). Without this, parameters compensate poorly, producing persistent mismatch across trajectories and time.
reflection.correct_approach: Extend ModelParameters and theta representation to support a small number of day buckets (e.g., 3–7) per disease: arrival_lambda[disease, bucket]. In HospitalFlowModel.rollout, compute bucket index from (day0+t) and use the corresponding lambda. Keep parameter count modest to preserve identifiability and generalization (shared buckets across splits). Update get_parameters_uniform_prior_min_max(), theta_to_parameters(), parameters_to_theta(), and theta_to_named_parameters() accordingly.
reflection.key_insight: When state trajectories are non-stationary, static arrival parameters will inflate occupancy/alive MSE; add low-dimensional time variation (bucketed rates) before increasing model complexity elsewhere.

blueprint_refs: Prefer empirical discrete distribution over observed initial los_remaining (day_in_hospital==1) to match integer nature.
assign initial los_remaining via calibrated LOS distributions conditional on disease_id and bed_type

evidence.metrics: Large errors in alive counts/occupancy suggest LOS-driven census dynamics are off; current calibrated los_mean values cluster around ~12–14 days but still do not reduce val_loss.

reflection.error_identification: Census dynamics (occupancy and alive counts) remain far from data even after calibration, indicating LOS sampling is structurally mismatched.
reflection.root_cause_analysis: HospitalFlowModel._sample_los uses a geometric distribution parameterized by mean. Real hospital LOS distributions are typically heavy-tailed and not memoryless, and the blueprint recommends using an empirical discrete distribution of initial los_remaining at admission (day_in_hospital==1) conditional on (disease, bed_type). The geometric assumption can distort the discharge hazard shape, producing systematic census errors that parameter tuning cannot fix.
reflection.correct_approach: Replace geometric LOS sampling with an empirical discrete sampler per (disease_id, bed_type) built from train data admissions (patients with day_in_hospital==1). Implement: (1) during data load or in a new preprocessing step (using existing parsed patients), build observed support values and probabilities for initial los_remaining by group; (2) store them inside the model (not as learnable neural params) or as calibratable simplex parameters with a small capped support; (3) in _sample_los, sample from this discrete distribution. Keep max_los consistent with observed support.
reflection.key_insight: If occupancy/alive errors persist after calibrating LOS means, the LOS distribution shape is wrong; model LOS with empirical discrete support at admission to match discharge dynamics.

blueprint_refs: Observation x_o (single-trajectory): use ONLY train_states[0] (trajectory_id=0) as the observation.
Evaluation: using optimized_parameters, evaluate on ALL trajectories from train/val/test

evidence.metrics: train_loss and val_loss are both extremely high and nearly equal (858.48 vs 862.25), suggesting parameters learned from a single observation are not informative enough to generalize, and/or calibration is ineffective.

reflection.error_identification: Learned parameters do not improve training or validation trajectory fit, indicating the single-trajectory observation provides weak identifiability for the current parameterization and/or inference method.
reflection.root_cause_analysis: Even though the blueprint mandates using train_states[0] as x_o, the simulator’s current parameterization (stationary arrivals + geometric LOS + single Gaussian posterior) likely makes many parameters weakly identifiable from a single trajectory, causing posterior collapse to average-ish values that don't fit any split well.
reflection.correct_approach: Keep x_o construction per blueprint, but improve identifiability by changing simulator structure (time-bucket arrivals; empirical LOS) and by adding simulator-in-the-loop selection at x_o (sample multiple theta candidates from learned q(theta|x_o) and choose theta that minimizes MSE on x_o’s trajectory summary). This preserves the blueprint’s single-observation rule while making the chosen theta actually fit the observation and transfer better.
reflection.key_insight: When constrained to a single observation trajectory, improve structural identifiability and add a final simulator-based selection step; otherwise inference can converge to parameters that satisfy the density model but not the trajectory metric.

blueprint_refs: optional mortality/early-exit is disabled by default unless strongly supported by data

evidence.metrics: Alive-count MSE is very large, but this is more likely driven by arrivals/LOS mismatch than mortality; still, mortality is implicitly fixed to always alive for new admissions.

reflection.error_identification: Mortality is effectively disabled (good), but the implementation removes patients only via LOS and checks p.is_alive without any explicit mechanism toggle, which can complicate future extensions and debugging of alive counts.
reflection.root_cause_analysis: HospitalFlowModel.rollout filters roster with `p.los_remaining > 0 and p.is_alive`, but there is no explicit mortality parameter/toggle in ModelParameters; new patients are always created with is_alive=True. This matches the default-off blueprint intent but is implicit rather than explicit, making it harder to verify alignment when data contains is_alive fields.
reflection.correct_approach: Add an explicit mortality toggle/parameter in ModelParameters (default off / zero hazard) only if needed, and ensure initialization from data preserves is_alive. Also add a short invariant/debug hook (optional) to verify that is_alive stays True when mortality is disabled, to avoid accidental changes affecting alive summaries.
reflection.key_insight: When a mechanism is 'disabled by default', keep it explicitly represented as a toggle with a no-op default so future changes don’t silently alter evaluation-relevant summaries.

blueprint_refs: Fit/eval computed on 7-D summary produced by trajectories_to_numpy()
assign initial los_remaining via calibrated LOS distributions conditional on disease_id and bed_type
assign each admitted patient a bed_type via calibrated probabilities

evidence.metrics: val_loss=36.044; val_loss_per_dim has large errors for d0_alive=72.72, d1_alive=74.09, total_alive=43.55; optimized los_mean for d1 ICU/Std and d2 ICU collapsed to 1.0; p_icu(d0)=0, p_icu(d1)=0, p_icu(d2)~0.99

reflection.error_identification: Validation MSE remains high and is dominated by alive-count dimensions. Multiple calibrated parameters hit bounds (LOS means collapse to 1; ICU routing collapses to 0/1), indicating the optimizer is compensating for structural mismatch rather than finding stable, generalizable dynamics.
reflection.root_cause_analysis: Current dynamics can only change alive counts through LOS-based discharge with a (mostly) stationary arrival model and fixed bed assignment. The extreme fitted parameters suggest the model cannot match disease-specific alive trajectories with just per-disease Poisson arrivals + a mean-scaled empirical LOS sampler, so it drives LOS to minimum and forces bed routing extremes to indirectly shape occupancy/alive counts. Likely missing: disease-specific LOS shape (not just mean scaling) and/or stronger nonstationarity/trajectory heterogeneity in arrivals than the global day-profile provides.
reflection.correct_approach: Within existing 12-parameter interface, reduce the need for extreme compensation by: (1) replacing mean-scaling of empirical LOS with a discrete reweighting scheme that preserves integer support but shifts mass smoothly (e.g., exponential tilting over observed LOS values) per (disease, bed) using the los_mean parameter as a control; this allows shape adaptation without collapsing to LOS=1. Implement in HospitalFlowModel._sample_los by computing tilted probabilities over info['values'] based on a temperature/tilt derived from target_mean vs empirical mean, then sample from tilted probs. (2) Make arrival nonstationarity disease-specific but also allow trajectory-level randomness: in HospitalFlowModel.rollout, draw a per-trajectory multiplicative random effect for each disease (mean 1, moderate variance) applied to arrival_lambda_for_day; this improves cross-trajectory generalization without changing theta dimensionality. Keep the effect deterministic given seed and trajectory_id to avoid training/val leakage.
reflection.key_insight: When calibrated parameters consistently hit bounds, treat it as evidence the simulator’s latent degrees of freedom (distribution shapes and heterogeneity) are insufficient; add shape/heterogeneity mechanisms before further tuning.

blueprint_refs: day_index used as a covariate for arrival rates and/or mixture weights by disease; optional
Evaluation: evaluate on ALL trajectories from train/val/test via existing evaluation functions

evidence.metrics: train_loss≈36.27, val_loss≈36.04 (no meaningful improvement vs prior best); alive-count errors remain very large

reflection.error_identification: Day-varying arrival modulation learned from the entire training set does not improve validation and can encode split-specific temporal structure that does not transfer, while also being non-parameterized (not part of θ) and therefore not properly inferred by SBI.
reflection.root_cause_analysis: HospitalFlowModel.ingest_training_statistics learns _arrival_profile_scale directly from train data and then uses it during both calibration and evaluation. This adds a strong, fixed, non-θ component to the simulator. Because SBI only infers θ, any data-derived profile acts like an unmodeled, hard-coded prior that may fit training idiosyncrasies and reduce identifiability/generalization.
reflection.correct_approach: Gate or simplify the arrival profile so it cannot overfit: (1) Change ingest_training_statistics to compute a single smooth seasonality curve shared across diseases (or a very low-rank representation) rather than a full length-T per-disease profile; keep it normalized to mean 1. (2) Add an on/off toggle (default off) for using _arrival_profile_scale during calibration/evaluation, and evaluate whether val_loss improves with it disabled. (3) If kept on, compute the profile from train_states[0] only (matching x_o) to avoid injecting information from other training trajectories into the simulator used for inference.
reflection.key_insight: Avoid injecting non-θ, data-derived dynamics into the simulator unless they are part of the inference target; otherwise SBI optimizes against a moving/hidden mechanism and generalization suffers.

blueprint_refs: Prefer empirical discrete distribution over observed initial los_remaining (day_in_hospital==1) to match integer nature

evidence.metrics: val_loss_per_dim: standard_occupancy=31.18 and total_alive=43.55 indicate discharge/occupancy timing mismatch

reflection.error_identification: Even with empirical LOS values, scaling individual draws by target_mean/emp_mean and rounding can create unrealistic LOS mass at 1 (or other small integers), changing discharge hazards and producing persistent occupancy/alive errors.
reflection.root_cause_analysis: In HospitalFlowModel._sample_los, LOS is sampled from empirical values then multiplied by a scale and rounded. This transforms the distribution in a non-smooth, value-dependent way and can concentrate probability mass at small integers after rounding/clipping, especially when target_mean is driven low by calibration.
reflection.correct_approach: Replace per-sample scaling with probability reweighting over the original empirical support: keep info['values'] unchanged, compute new probabilities proportional to probs * f(values; tilt) where tilt is chosen to match (approximately) the desired mean implied by los_mean, then sample directly from values. Maintain clipping to [1, max_los] but avoid rounding a scaled value.
reflection.key_insight: For discrete time-to-exit processes, adjust distribution via probability tilting on the original integer support rather than scaling sampled values and rounding.

blueprint_refs: Train NPE posterior p(θ|x) on simulated pairs; then condition on x_o, sample posterior, and take posterior mean as optimized_parameters.

evidence.metrics: Calibration loss_history decreases to ~0.95 but val_loss remains ~36, indicating good surrogate fit does not translate to better trajectory MSE

reflection.error_identification: The calibrator’s neural surrogate training objective (Gaussian NLL on standardized θ) improves substantially, but downstream evaluation MSE does not improve, implying the inferred θ is not well-aligned with minimizing trajectory MSE.
reflection.root_cause_analysis: Blueprint expects an SBI posterior; current implementation uses a diagonal Gaussian posterior surrogate and then performs a heuristic candidate search. This can be poorly calibrated for multi-modal or heteroscedastic posteriors and can overemphasize matching θ distribution rather than directly optimizing x reconstruction. Candidate selection uses only train_states[0] flattened MSE, which can still select θ that overfits the single observation and generalizes poorly.
reflection.correct_approach: Keep the same structure but align selection more robustly: (1) during candidate selection, score each candidate not only on x_o MSE but also on a small set of auxiliary summaries computed from x (e.g., per-dimension time-averages/variances derived from the same 7-D array) to reduce degenerate fits; implement inside NPEGaussianCalibrator.fit without changing outputs. (2) Increase stochastic averaging for the score: for each candidate θ, run multiple rollouts with different RNG substreams (seeded deterministically from θ hash + base seed) and score the mean MSE; this reduces selecting lucky noise fits and improves validation stability.
reflection.key_insight: If posterior learning is approximate, selecting θ should be noise-robust and summary-aware; otherwise the selector overfits a single noisy rollout and won’t improve validation.
